source.title: Attention Misses Visual Risk: Risk-Adaptive Steering for Multimodal Safety Alignment
source.authors: Jonghyun Park; Minhyuk Seo; Chaewon Yeo; Jonghyun Choi

record.tranche_reason: The study compares activation steering with the safe/unsafe difference-in-means refusal vector cited from the original work, and reports resulting attack success rates. It does not test ablation.
record.gate_note: Table 7 reports the relevant steering comparison and is recorded below. The attention and FDR analyses compare safe/unsafe representations but do not measure refusal caused by the difference-in-means direction, so they are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: Supplementary Sec. 8 / Table 7 adds the Arditi-style difference-in-means vector (unsafe minus safe means) to LLaVA-1.5-7B activations and reports jailbreak ASR on five multimodal benchmarks. This is a new setting (multimodal model, jailbreak inputs) that bears on V1's 'adding the direction induces refusal' part. It is not T1: the vector is taken at response-token positions, scaled by the MoRAS risk score r(S), and applied only to the first 3 tokens. The measure is ASR judged by MD-Judge, not refusal or harmful-compliance scores. The rest of the paper is a defense method (T4-like) and the attention/FDR analyses do not measure the direction's effect.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two additions. The comparison was run inside MoRAS: steering is scaled by the risk score and applied to the first 3 response tokens. The authors conclude that the Arditi-style global vector gives only modest safety gains (average ASR 36.6% at layer 14, 25.9% at the last layer). Their query-adaptive vector gives 13.1% and 8.3%, and the unsafe query set matters little compared with global vs adaptive formulation.
record.recipe_differences: The study implements activation steering using the cited safe/unsafe difference-in-means vector, but tests steering rather than projection ablation and compares it with an input-specific vector. It evaluates multimodal jailbreak ASR rather than the full original set of refusal and capability outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with steering layer (14 versus last), vector formulation (global versus input-specific), unsafe prototype source (mixed datasets versus GPT-4), and benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: A query-specific steering vector toward the mean unsafe-response activation (μu − h, risk-scaled) cuts ASR more than the global diff-in-means vector: average 13.1% vs 36.6% at layer 14, and 8.3% vs 25.9% at the last layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MLLMs, pulling activations toward a refusal prototype point induces refusal on jailbreak inputs more reliably than adding a fixed diff-in-means refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Safe and unsafe multimodal queries with identical text have low Fisher discriminant ratio across layers in LLaVA-1.5-7B, attributed to weak attention to unsafe image regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLLM failure to refuse image-embedded harm stems from poor harmful/harmless separability in activations, not from a missing refusal mechanism.

record.problems: The global-vector comparison reports ASR only; it does not directly measure refusal rates on harmless requests or general capability under that vector. No uncertainty estimates are given for Table 7. The intervention is not ablation.

untested.parts: Directional ablation and removal of refusal. Effect of the added direction on harmless prompts. Capability preservation under the Eq. 8 vector. Unscaled fixed-strength addition at instruction positions.
Not tested. Comparing a global direction with a query-specific pull toward a target point says nothing about affine, cone or multi-direction refusal geometry.

record.verdict_notes: Only Supplementary Table 7 bears on the claim. The Eq. 8 vector is computed at response-token positions and its strength is multiplied by r(S), so the test is not a clean fixed-direction addition. No uncertainty is reported. No harmless-prompt or utility numbers are given for Eq. 8. The record's V4 linking was removed: Eq. 9 is the authors' own method, not evidence about refusal geometry.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not project the direction out, test ablation at every layer and position, measure refusal on harmless requests after adding the direction, or evaluate whether abilities are preserved under the global difference-in-means vector.
The study compares a global mean-difference vector with an input-specific vector, but does not test affine or cone geometries, or whether a dominant direction coexists with other fixed directions.

relationships.condition: LLaVA-1.5-7B, Eq. 8 diff-in-means addition (risk-scaled, first 3 response tokens) on JOOD at layer 14, and on FigStep/MM-Safety/JOOD at the last layer with GPT-4 unsafe means
relationships.reason: ASR falls to about 8–12% from vanilla 40–60% (t7-eq8-l14-mix-jood, t7-eq8-l14-gpt-jood, t7-eq8-last-gpt-figstep, t7-eq8-last-gpt-mms, t7-eq8-last-gpt-jood).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success fell from approximately 40–60% to 8–12% under the tested direction-addition settings.

relationships.condition: Same Eq. 8 addition at layer 14 (Arditi's layer) on SPA-VL/FigStep/MM-Safety/VAA, and at the last layer on the remaining benchmarks
relationships.reason: Only partial ASR reductions, and almost none for FigStep at layer 14 (59.3→56.8/57.8). Effect depends on layer and unsafe-set choice; authors call the gains 'only modest' (averages 36.6% L14, 25.9% last). Rows t7-eq8-l14-*-spa/figstep/mms/vaa and t7-eq8-last-mix-*, t7-eq8-last-gpt-spa/vaa.
relationships.display_finding: FigStep ASR fell only from 59.3 to 56.8 or 57.8 at layer 14, with reported averages of 36.6% at layer 14 and 25.9% at the last layer.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Global difference-in-means steering at layer 14 or the last layer, with mixed or GPT-4 unsafe prototypes
reader_labels.reason: Steering reduces ASR in these conditions but leaves attacks successful; this is partial evidence for a refusal effect, not evidence that the direction fully mediates refusal. Rows t7-eq8-l14-mix-spa through t7-eq8-last-gpt-vaa.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Global mean-difference vector compared with input-specific steering
reader_labels.reason: The global vector generally gives weaker ASR reductions than the input-specific vector, although the global vector still reduces ASR; the study compares these formulations but does not test affine or cone geometry. Rows t7-eq8-l14-mix-spa through t7-eq8-last-gpt-vaa.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Input-specific vector steering at layer 14 or the last layer
reader_labels.reason: The input-specific vector yields lower ASR than the matched global-vector formulation in most reported comparisons; authors conclude query-adaptive directions are more effective. Rows t7-eq9-l14-mix-spa through t7-eq9-last-gpt-vaa.
